# Eski Lua runtime

This component embeds upstream Lua through an original protected C shim. The Odin binding selects release/address/thread archives from the .build/lua layout.

The ABI is `include/eslua.h` with a matching `include/eslua_ffi.odin`. All sizes use C size_t, counters use uint64_t, status/action/protocol fields use int32_t, and callbacks use the C calling convention.

`eslua_eval` executes source in a fresh VM with binary-safe KEYS/ARGV, a separate final client RESP version and caller callbacks. `eslua_compile` syntax-checks source in a protected fresh VM and returns `+OK` or an error frame without running user code. `eslua_version` names the runtime. Top-level result data is owned by C; call `eslua_free_result` exactly once even for errors. The result always describes one RESP frame when data is nonnull. A null data pointer with nonzero status is a terminal allocation failure and must become a fixed host error.

Command callback arguments include the command name. Their bytes are borrowed until the callback returns and must not be retained. `resp` is the script's current redis.setresp choice, independent of the final caller protocol. The callback returns borrowed RESP bytes; the host must retain the latest response until the next command-callback entry or eslua_eval returns. It may free the previous response at that next entry. The decoder copies strings into Lua and retains no host pointers; an allocation error abandons the C parsing frame, so retaining the latest response through the next boundary also covers skipped per-call cleanup. Busy/log callbacks do not end this lifetime. Status0 means an ordinary command response, including RESP error frames handled by call/pcall. A nonzero callback status is a sticky host failure. write_effect is nonzero whenever an actual write/effect occurred, including before an error. The callback must never invoke any Lua API or throw across C.

The busy callback receives write state and a stats snapshot; CONTINUE does nothing, KILL_READONLY aborts only if no write has occurred, and ABORT is an unconditional explicit host policy deviation. Standard no-save process abort belongs to the host. The callback must use restricted service only: no normal event loop or command reentry. The log callback receives borrowed string/number arguments and returns normally.

Stats current_bytes/peak_bytes include bounded runtime-owned VM and conversion regions, not the host's command-response arenas or source cache. At a callback they describe current occupancy; a top-level result reports zero live VM bytes after cleanup and the invocation peak. Returned output remains owned until free_result. Elapsed_ns is monotonic wall time; instructions is hook-accounted approximate instruction fuel.

memory_limit/output_limit/max_depth/hook_count zero select64MiB/16MiB/64/1000 defaults. instruction_limit0 disables the optional hard instruction budget; busy_threshold_ms0 disables threshold service. An explicit hard instruction limit can abort after writes; it is separate from standard BUSY/KILL semantics. Use normal busy threshold semantics unless the host documents that policy. Limits are requested allocation bytes, not RSS. Source+KEYS+ARGV payload lengths are also limited by memory_limit before VM setup. Null input pointers are accepted only for zero-length strings. If no bounded error frame can be allocated, a nonzero status can have null data and the host must synthesize its fixed error.

The host owns command lookup/ACL/read-only policy, AOF effects/atomicity, source cache/digests and BUSY network authentication/lifetime. No Lua API or longjmp may cross an Odin callback. Only C code constructs Lua values or raises Lua errors, and all allocation-capable Lua API work is protected.

Original helper scope: cjson encode/decode/null, cmsgpack pack/unpack, the signed32 bit facade, SHA1, RESP2/3 conversions, redis.call/pcall/status_reply/error_reply/log/sha1hex/setresp and replicate_commands()=>true. No bit32 global is exposed: Lua5.2 bit32 has different unsigned/shift behavior and additional functions. set_repl raises an unsupported error. The codec namespaces are compatibility subsets, with no cjson tuning/new API or MessagePack extension support. JSON requires valid UTF-8, finite numbers and string object keys; empty tables encode as objects. MessagePack accepts concatenated packed values, standard scalar/str/bin/array/map tags and encodes empty tables as arrays. Unpacking an empty MessagePack stream returns zero values; truncated or unsupported frames remain errors. Native Lua5.5 integer/numeric/iteration behavior is not Lua5.1 equivalence. Unordered maps retain Lua iteration order.

Boolean returns first follow the script's protocol: default RESP2 converts false to null and true to integer1, including for a RESP3 client. After redis.setresp(3), they are native booleans for RESP3 clients and integer0/1 when downgraded to RESP2. A Lua nil remains null.

An uncaught redis.call command error preserves its host error code. Global pcall still receives that error as a Lua string; catching it ends the host-origin marker, so an explicit later error() is an ordinary Lua exception. Ordinary uncaught Lua exceptions receive an ERR prefix even when their text already begins with ERR. A thrown table with a string err field is recognized without invoking metamethods, like a returned error table. The error_reply helper normalizes empty text to ERR followed by a space; a directly returned table with an empty err string preserves that empty string. Error frames replace CR/LF with spaces; uncaught exception text is limited to4096bytes. Lua numeric command arguments remove a trailing .0 from their native number representation and canonicalize numeric negative zero to0, while explicit string arguments retain their exact bytes, including '-0' and '-0.0'. These conversions affect host argument bytes without changing Lua arithmetic.

Each fresh VM seeds math.random with monotonic nanoseconds and an atomic invocation counter before user code runs. This avoids repeating the default fresh-VM sequence across calls made within one second; it is not a cryptographic randomness guarantee. Explicit math.randomseed calls remain deterministic under the pinned Lua runtime.

Source cache/shebang/ACL/readonly policy belongs to the Odin host. The host hashes original bytes, validates a supported #!lua header and may pass newline-prefixed remaining source to preserve line numbers. Runtime loading is always text-only. A custom hard-fuel abort is sticky through pcall/xpcall; memory-budget failure is also sticky. C library helpers execute between instruction hooks, so the hook is cooperative rather than a preemptive wall-time guarantee.

The pinned upstream Lua source and its copyright text are preserved under vendor/lua-5.5.1; LICENSE.lua reproduces that release's notice. Four official upstream C patches are applied, with original complete patches and source-only applied extracts retained under patches. Upstream test hunks are retained for provenance and are not applied to the runtime. Runtime/shim/codec code is an original implementation and contains no Redis implementation code. The caller must separately preserve the project's licence for original files and the Lua MIT notice when distributing linked artifacts.
